scenes.title: 1983 Munich Clinic Table: Patient L.M. Pouring Tea That Appears Frozen Like a Glass Rod Until Overflowing Across the Saucer
scenes.era: 1983, Max Planck Institute for Psychiatry, Munich

layout.description: Sunlit 1983 Munich clinical testing room with a clean pale-oak table holding a matte-white porcelain teapot tilted in mid-pour above a porcelain teacup and saucer — where a crystal-clear translucent amber column hangs visually 'frozen' like a glass icicle until overflowing onto the white saucer — beside Josef Zihl's velocity-threshold perimeter screen.

positions.who: Patient L.M. (mannequin in 1983 tailored knit cardigan and collared blouse)
positions.where: holding the tilted white porcelain teapot with both hands, staring intently at the motionless-looking amber pour column and gasping only when tea spills over the saucer rim

positions.who: Josef Zihl (mannequin in 1983 white clinical coat and spectacles)
positions.where: seated across the table holding a stopwatch and smooth-pursuit velocity chart ('14°/s Lost')

props.name: white porcelain teapot, overflowing teacup & saucer
props.period_detail: captures L.M.'s immortal 'frozen like a glacier' pouring test
props.physical_behavior: neurology's single clearest real-world demonstration of V5 loss

props.name: moving light-target velocity board ('Smooth 14°/s')
props.period_detail: quantifies the exact velocity cliff discovered at Munich

actions.verb_sequence: tilts the porcelain teapot carefully watching the spout -> fails to detect rising cup motion until liquid brims over onto the saucer -> sets pot down startled
tests L.M. with eyes closed tracking a moving sound source left-to-right -> L.M. points smoothly and accurately!

reactions.reaction: relieved discovering her hearing and touch track motion 100% normally
maps symmetrical lateral temporo-occipital V5 lesions on the 1983 Brain diagram

scenes.wardrobe: 1983 German clinical coat with tie; neat wool cardigan over collared blouse.
scenes.lighting: Clean high-key European window daylight catching the glassy amber tea stream.
scenes.recognition_hook: To her sharp 20/20 eyes, hot tea pouring out of a spout looks frozen solid like a glass rod — until a puddle suddenly appears on the table.

key_visual.description: a 1983 Munich clinic table where a seated woman pours from a white porcelain teapot into an overflowing teacup beside a neurologist holding a velocity threshold chart

scenes.title: Strobe-Frame Street Crossing: Far Away, Then Instantly Here
scenes.era: 1983, Sunlit Munich crosswalk model / window view

layout.description: Bright clinic window overlooking a quiet tree-lined street and tabletop traffic-speed model.

positions.where: practicing listening to smooth engine Doppler sound instead of trusting discrete visual car jumps

props.name: tabletop street-crossing distance model
props.period_detail: illustrates why >14°/s cars seem to teleport without smooth visual approach

actions.verb_sequence: trains L.M. to wait and judge acoustic engine sweep before stepping off curb

reactions.reaction: crosses confidently using intact auditory motion

scenes.recognition_hook: Look down the block and the car is 100 yards away — blink, and without V5 it teleports straight to the crosswalk.

scenes.title: 1991 Eight-Year Follow-Up: Pouring Perfectly by Ear!

layout.description: Bright tidy kitchen table with a porcelain teapot and ceramic mug.

positions.where: tilting her ear slightly toward the mug as she pours, stopping crisply 1 cm below the rim by listening to the rising resonant pitch!

props.name: tall ceramic mug & teapot
props.period_detail: acoustic resonance rises in pitch as air column shortens
props.physical_behavior: Zihl et al. 1991 documented everyday triumph

actions.verb_sequence: pours steadily while listening -> stops right at the top with zero spill

reactions.reaction: calm, proud smile of adaptive mastery

scenes.recognition_hook: Anyone can test L.M.'s secret right now: close your eyes at a water tap and hear the rising pitch announce 'full!' right on time.

scenes.title: Reversible 50-ms Motion Freeze via V5 TMS (Beckers & Zeki)

layout.description: Clean TMS suite with a random-dot motion screen and handheld coil.

positions.where: watching moving dots freeze for a split second strictly during a lateral V5 magnetic pulse while dot color stays crisp

props.name: dot-motion monitor & V5 TMS coil
props.period_detail: replicates L.M.'s dissociation reversibly in healthy brains

actions.verb_sequence: triggers 50-ms V5 pulse -> motion freezes briefly then resumes smoothly

reactions.reaction: marvels that shape and color never flickered

scenes.recognition_hook: Pause area V5 for one twentieth of a second in a healthy brain, and motion freezes while color and sharpness never blink.
